name: com.structomat/steel
title: Structomat
description: Steel structures: 3D frame analysis, AISC checks, IFC cost, tonnage, connections, LGS house design.

tools.name: about_structomat
tools.description: Facts about Structomat, an AI engineering agent for structural steel: what it does, design codes, who signs designs for construction, what to send, what comes back, NDA and file ownership, how to start. Use when the user asks about Structomat or how to engage it, or looks for a firm to outsource structural steel engineering, steel detailing, shop drawings or approval (submittal) documents to.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Structomat services (analysis & design, connection design, shop drawings, erectability check of a steel model before erection, automation consulting, custom tools) with what the client sends and what comes back.

tools.name: find_examples
tools.description: Search Structomat's published work: steel projects, case studies, example situations, checked steel connections, measured benchmarks (e.g. scan-to-BIM from a point cloud), sample deliverables (e.g. a complete US AISC shop drawing submittal with a clouded revision, or an erectability check that finds the pieces of a clash-free model that cannot get into place during erection) and free tools. Returns titles, links and short summaries.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "canopy", "mezzanine", "base plate", "HEB 600", "crane", "point cloud".

tools.name: get_connection
tools.description: Details of one connection from the Structomat steel connection library: members, plates, bolts, welds, design code and the utilisation of each component. Use find_examples with type "connection" to get slugs.

tools.name: estimate_portal_frame_steel
tools.description: Steel tonnage estimate for a single-span pitched portal frame building (span 15-30 m) before any design: total tonnes, kg per m2 of floor, a range, the weight by part (frames, gable posts, bracing, eave struts, purlins, side rails, plates and connections) and typical member sizes. Interpolated between complete finite-element designs and calibrated against published designs. Use for budgets, tenders and feasibility; a real design needs the actual loads and code.

span_m.description: Clear span of the frames, m (15-30).

length_m.description: Building length, m. Frames are at 6 m.

ground_snow_kN_m2.description: Characteristic ground snow load sk, kN/m2 (0.5-2.0). Roof load = 0.8 sk.

bracing.description: Optional: tube (default, tension and compression) or tension-only rods.

tools.name: analyze_frame
tools.description: Runs a 3D finite-element frame analysis and returns the numbers: equilibrium check, largest deflection along the members, largest joint displacement and sway in X and Y, every support reaction, the axial force, shears and moments of every member (the envelope with the governing combination when there are several), and natural periods with mass participation (modal analysis); linear or second order (P-Delta). The model is either a template (a pitched portal frame building, an open mono-pitch canopy, or a multi-storey frame, from a few dimensions, sections and loads) or a full model in JSON (nodes, members, sections, supports, loads, combinations). It is solved by the code of Structomat's free 3D frame analysis page, so the result also has a link that shows the same model and results in 3D (deflected shape, force diagrams, mode shapes). Use it to check a frame, compare sections or see how loads flow, and run it again with changed sections or loads. The result also has a preliminary member check to AISC 360-16 LRFD (results.member_check): the demand-to-capacity ratio of each member with the governing check, combination and point, for IPE, HEA, HEB, CHS and SHS sections and I or tube sections with dimensions; effective length factor K = 1 and unbraced length Lb = member length unless set (beam_unbraced_m, column_unbraced_m, or "check" on a model member). The forces are elastic second order without notional loads or stiffness reduction (not the direct analysis method): K = 1 holds only when the second-order sway is at most 1.1 times the linear sway, otherwise K must come from a stability analysis; a linear run gives no valid check; connections, seismic provisions and fire are not covered, and code load combinations only through combination_set. The model is not stored.

template.description: portal = pitched portal frame building; mono = open mono-pitch canopy; storey = multi-storey frame. Omit when sending model.

low_height_m.description: mono: height of the low side, m.

high_height_m.description: mono: height of the high side, m.

span_m.description: portal (4-60) or mono (3-30): frame span, m.

ridge_rise_m.description: portal: ridge rise above eave, m.

bays_z.description: storey: bays in Y (the second horizontal direction; Z is vertical).

bay_x_m.description: storey: bay width in X, m.

bay_z_m.description: storey: bay width in Y, m.

brace_section.description: portal, mono: hollow section for the bracing (default CHS 139.7x5).

column_web.description: Direction of the column webs: x (default) = strong axis resists sway in X, the frame direction; y = strong axis resists sway in Y.

wind_direction.description: portal, storey: x (default) = wind on the long wall / the face at X = 0; y = wind on the gable / the face at Y = 0; xy = both together in the same combination (conservative).

combination_set.description: single (default) = one combination with the factors given; en = a typical EN 1990 ultimate set (expression 6.10); asce = ASCE 7 LRFD basic combinations. en and asce are solved as an envelope.

modal.description: Also run a modal analysis: natural periods, mode shapes and mass participation (default true).

modal_live_share.description: Share of the live or snow load in the modal mass, psi (default 0.3); mass = self-weight + dead + psi x live.

dead_kN_m2.description: Dead load on roof/floor, kN/m2 (self-weight of members is added).

wind_kN_m2.description: portal, storey: wind pressure on the windward face (see wind_direction); mono: net wind pressure on the roof, positive upward (uplift); kN/m2.

leeward_kN_m2.description: portal, storey: leeward suction, kN/m2 (not used for mono).

steel_grade.description: Steel for the member check: S235, S275, S355 (default; S..H for tubes) or ASTM (A992 for I-sections, A500 Gr. C for tubes).

beam_unbraced_m.description: portal, mono, storey: unbraced length Lb of the beams / rafters for lateral-torsional buckling in the member check, m (spacing of purlins or other restraints of the compression flange; default the member length).

column_unbraced_m.description: portal, mono, storey: unbraced length Lb of the columns in the member check, m (spacing of girts or other restraints; default the member length).

model.description: Instead of a template: a full model, units kN and m, Z vertical. {"up":"Z", "nodes":{"N1":[x,y,z],...}, "members":[{"id":"M1","i":"N1","j":"N2","sec":"S1","rot":0,"pinned":false}], "sections":{"S1":{"A":m2,"Iy":m4 weak,"Iz":m4 strong,"J":m4}}, "supports":{"N1":"fixed"|"pinned"}, "nodeLoads":[{"node":"N2","case":"G"|"Q"|"W","F":[Fx,Fy,Fz]}], "memberLoads":[{"member":"M1","case":"G","dir":"FX"|"FY"|"FZ","w":kN_per_m}], "combos":[{"name":"ULS1","factors":{"G":1.35,"Q":1.5}}], "selfWeight":true, "analysis":"pdelta"|"linear", "modal":{"modes":12,"G":1,"Q":0.3}}. Load cases may have any name; several combinations are solved and shown with their envelope (a single "combo":{...} is still accepted). Gravity loads act in -FZ. A member load may vary from w to w2 between x1 and x2 (m from the i end). "pinned": true releases bending at both ends, "i" or "j" at one end. The modal mass may use any load case, e.g. {"modes":12,"G":1,"S":0.3}. A vertical member has its web (local axis 2) along X; "rot":90 turns it to Y. Without "up":"Z" the older format with Y vertical is read and converted. Steel E = 210 GPa. Member check: give each section a standard "name" (e.g. "HEA 300", "CHS 139.7x5", "SHS 100x100x5") or it is analysed but not checked; a member may carry "check":{"Lcx":m,"Lcy":m,"Lcz":m,"Lb":m} (Lcx about the strong axis, Lcz torsional, default the member length); a member with a free end is checked as a cantilever (Cb = 1.0).

tools.name: check_steel_members
tools.description: Preliminary strength check of steel members to AISC 360-16 LRFD under the forces you give: available strengths and the demand-to-capacity ratio D/C of each member, the governing limit state and every step with its clause. Covers compression (flexural, torsional and local buckling, E3/E4/E7), tension yielding (D2), bending about both axes with lateral-torsional and local buckling (F2, F3, F6, F7, F8; Cb given or from the moment diagram, 1.0 for cantilevers), shear (G2.1, G4, G5, G6) and the H1-1 interaction, for I-sections (IPE, HEA, HEB, or dimensions: rolled when a root radius r > 0 is given, welded when r = 0 or "built_up": true), rectangular and square hollow sections (RHS/SHS) and round hollow sections (CHS), HSS design wall thickness 0.93t (B4.2). Steel grades ASTM A992, A36, A572 Gr. 50, A500 Gr. C, A53 Gr. B, or Fy; EN S235-S355 (EN 10025, EN 10219 as S..H) are checked with the AISC equations by analogy, since AISC 360-16 approves ASTM materials (A3.1a). The forces are taken as given: they must include second-order effects, from the direct analysis method of Chapter C or, with K from a stability analysis, the effective length method (analyze_frame gives elastic second-order forces without notional loads or stiffness reduction, and its result already has a member check of every member); the effective lengths are yours. Not covered (reported): webs noncompact or slender in flexure for I-sections, torsion, net-section rupture, connections, seismic provisions, fire. Up to 50 members per call; nothing is stored.

section.description: A name: "IPE 300", "HEA 200", "HEB 400", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6", "CHS 139.7x5"; or dimensions in mm: {"shape":"I","h":..,"b":..,"tw":..,"tf":..,"r":..} (r = 0 or "built_up": true = welded), {"shape":"RHS","h":..,"b":..,"t":..}, {"shape":"CHS","D":..,"t":..}.

grade.description: Steel grade (default S355). EN Fy by thickness to EN 1993-1-1 Table 3.1.

Lcx_m.description: Effective length for buckling about the strong axis, Lc = K L, m (default L).

Lcy_m.description: Effective length for buckling about the weak axis, m (default L).

Lcz_m.description: Effective length for torsional buckling, m (default L, independent of Lcy).

Lb_m.description: Unbraced length for lateral-torsional buckling, m (default L).

Cb.description: Lateral-torsional buckling modification factor (default 1.0, or from cb_moments_kNm; F1-1 limited to 3.0 by this tool). Use 1.0 for a cantilever with an unbraced free end (F1).

cb_moments_kNm.description: [Mmax, MA, MB, MC] of the unbraced segment (F1-1) to compute Cb.

N_kN.description: Required axial force, kN: tension positive, compression negative.

M_major_kNm.description: Required moment about the strong axis, kNm.

M_minor_kNm.description: Required moment about the weak axis, kNm.

V_major_kN.description: Required shear parallel to the web (with strong-axis bending), kN.

V_minor_kN.description: Required shear in the other direction, kN.

T_kNm.description: Torsion, kNm: not checked, only flagged.

cantilever.description: true for a cantilever with an unbraced free end: Cb = 1.0 (F1).

tools.name: estimate_steel_cost
tools.description: Cost of fabricating and erecting a steel structure, worked out part by part from its IFC model: every part, hole, weld and lift is timed as a shop or site operation and priced at the region's employer labour cost, steel price and crane rate. Returns the cost floor (total, per tonne, per m2 of floor) with its breakdown, the published market band next to it and the gap, the process groups that drive the cost, the ten costliest parts with their IFC ids, a programme from shop drawings to erection in working days, upfront embodied carbon (modules A1-A5: steel production, fabrication, delivery, erection), and what an example design review (lighter sections, fewer plate fittings) would save in cost and carbon. Regions: UK, DE (Germany), US, AU, or own rates in any currency. Give the IFC as a public link (ifc_url, up to 30 MB) or as its text (ifc_text, up to 12 MB), or sample=true for a sample 18 x 30 m portal frame shed. It is the engine of Structomat's free Steel Cost Estimator page, which shows the same result with a 3D cost heat map when the same IFC is dropped on it. An estimate, not a quote. The IFC is read in memory and not stored.

ifc_url.description: Public http(s) link to the IFC file (IFC2x3 or IFC4, up to 30 MB).

ifc_text.description: The IFC file content as text (STEP, starting with ISO-10303-21), up to 12 MB. Use instead of ifc_url.

sample.description: true = use the sample building (18 x 30 m portal frame shed, 799 parts) instead of an IFC.

region.description: Labour, steel and crane rates and the market band: UK (GBP), DE (EUR), US (USD), AU (AUD), or own = your rates in "rates". Default UK.

rates.description: Optional overrides of the region's rates (required for region "own"): currency code, eur_rate = 1 EUR in that currency, shop_wage and site_wage = employer cost per hour worked (not a sell rate), steel_per_t, crane_per_day (with operator), overhead_pct, profit_pct.

market_price_per_t.description: region "own": the market price per tonne you see, to show the gap to the floor.

shop.description: mixed (default) = automated saw-drill line and plate cutting plus handling and marking; cnc = machine times only; manual = conventional shop.

erection.description: norms (default) = crew man-hours by section class; cycle = crane lift cycles per piece (reads low on single-storey sheds).

floor_area_m2.description: Gross floor area, m2. Default: the column grid found in the model.

carbon_route.description: Steel route for embodied carbon: bof = blast furnace mix, eaf = electric arc (recycled). Default eaf for US, bof elsewhere.

programme.description: Programme inputs in working days: drawing_days (shop drawings + approval, default 10), lead_days (steel lead time, default 10), shop_crew (default 4).

design_review.description: Example design review: steel_saved_pct (default 10) and plate_fittings_removed_pct (default 25, smallest plates first).

tools.name: design_lgs_framing
tools.description: Preliminary design of the cold-formed steel (light gauge steel, LGS) framing of a single-storey house with a gable roof on a concrete slab, in Canada: NBC 2020 Part 4 loads (snow, wind, earthquake when Sa values are given), members and screw connections to AISI S100-16 with the Canadian Appendix B (CSA S136) and AISI S240-20, Limit States Design. Frames the house (studs and tracks at 406 or 610 mm in line with Fink roof trusses, box headers with jack and king studs over every opening, full-height gable walls, bridging), analyses it and checks every member group and connection: truss chords, webs, heel and ridge gusset plates and screw groups, studs under axial load and wind, headers, gable wall studs, Type I OSB shear walls, the roof diaphragm, overall uplift and overturning. Sections not given are sized automatically (lightest SSMA S-section that passes; 43 mil and thicker studs). Returns the sections, piece count and steel mass by section, the governing utilisation ratio of each group and the ratio of every check, and which checks are conditional. Rectangular plan only, no interior load-bearing walls, roof 10 to 45 degrees, truss span 4 to 14 m, low building for wind. When wind uplift or overturning exceeds 0.9 x dead load the result says that anchorage to the foundation is required. Anchors, hold-down products, foundations, sheathing products and roll-former data are not designed. Nothing is stored. Preliminary, not signed.

length_m.description: Plan length, out-to-out of the wall framing, m. The front and back walls run along the length.

width_m.description: Plan width, m. The left and right walls run along the width.

wall_height_m.description: Wall height from the slab to the top of the wall framing, m.

roof_pitch.description: Roof slope as rise:run text ("6:12") or degrees (10 to 45). Default "6:12".

ridge_along.description: Ridge direction (default the longer side). The trusses span the other side and bear on the two eave walls.

spacing_mm.description: Stud and truss spacing, mm: 406 (16 in) or 610 (24 in, default).

openings.description: Doors and windows (default none). position_m = distance from the left end of the wall, seen from outside, to the side of the opening; at least 0.3 m from each corner and between openings.

sill_height_m.description: Windows: sill height above the slab, m (default 0.914).

head_height_m.description: Top of the opening above the slab, m (default 2.134; at most the wall height minus 0.25 m).

loads.description: Climatic data for the location from NBC 2020 Appendix C Table C-2, and seismic data from the NRCan 2020 seismic hazard tool.

seismic.description: Optional: 5% damped spectral acceleration Sa(T) in g for site designation X450 (Site Class C), 2% in 50 years. Without it the earthquake is NOT checked.

dead_loads.description: Optional dead loads, kPa: roof_kPa (roofing, sheathing, trusses, on plan; default 0.50), ceiling_kPa (default 0.35), wall_kPa (exterior wall, default 0.45).

sections.description: Optional fixed SSMA S-sections (e.g. "600S162-43"); the others are sized automatically. header = each of the two members of the box header.

stud_depth_in.description: Optional stud depth, in, when the wall thickness is fixed (default 6, then 8 if needed).

include_geometry.description: Also return the 3D geometry of every member (axis end points in mm, orientation, section, governing check) in structuredContent.geometry, for drawing the framing. Adds about 30 KB; default false.

tools.name: draft_project_request
tools.description: Prepare an e-mail to Structomat (info@structomat.com) describing a project, ready for the user to review and send. This tool sends nothing and stores nothing; it returns the draft text and a mailto link.

need.description: What the user needs, e.g. "structural analysis and calculation report for a 12 x 6 m steel canopy".

structure_type.description: Optional: canopy, mezzanine, warehouse, stair, connection, ...

design_code.description: Optional: Eurocode, AISC 360 or the code the project requires.

available_files.description: Optional: drawings, photos, IFC or analysis model the user can send.

tools.name: check_connection
tools.description: Instant utilisation (demand/capacity) of a standard steel connection under the given member-end forces, from capacities precomputed with finite-element connection analysis to AISC 360-16 LRFD (S275 steel, grade 8.8 bolts, C30/37 concrete). Returns the utilisation, the governing component (and the governing plate, weld or bolt group) and warnings. Call without "template" to list the templates and sizes. Forces are member-end forces at the analysis node, i.e. at the centreline of the supporting column or main beam (as a frame analysis gives them), not at its face; the capacities already include the offset. Only for a joint where no other member frames in: if anything else connects at the node, the result does not apply (ask for a connection design instead). For a first idea of a connection; a design for construction needs a checked calculation.

template.description: Connection template. Omit to list templates and sizes.

members.description: Section of each member by role, e.g. {"column": "HEA300", "beam": "IPE330"}.

N_kN.description: Member-end force at the node, kN: the force the loaded member applies to the connection, in member axes (x away from the node). Positive = tension (pulls away from the node).

Vy_kN.description: Base plate only: horizontal shear along the column flanges, kN.

Vz_kN.description: Beams: vertical shear the beam applies to the connection, kN, positive UPWARDS (gravity shear is negative). Base plate: horizontal shear along the column web.

My_kNm.description: Major-axis moment at the node, kNm (moment templates only). Positive = top flange of the beam in tension (hogging).

other_members_at_node.description: true if any other member (brace, second beam, etc.) connects at the same node.
